records.text: A Yahoo News report said Superfeed Technologies had its Arizona business status revoked while employing Jeff DeWit and paying Kari Lake more than 100,000 dollars as disclosed in her financial filing
records.speaker: Candace Owens

appearances.snippet: Kari Lake's bribery scandal involves a shady GOP tech firm. Yeah, they're referring to Superfeed Technologies had its business revoked by the state of Arizona while it employed Jeff DeWitt, its former COO, and Lake, who had received more than $100,000 from the entity in the personal financial disclosure that she filed last month.

verification.notes: The underlying Daily Beast report, republished in Yahoo-linked coverage, states Superfeed's Arizona authority was revoked in December 2021 for missed annual reports while Jeff DeWit and Kari Lake worked there, and that a disclosure showed Lake received 01,507. The company was later reinstated, which does not negate the historical claim.

links.title: Superfeed Scandal Does Not Prove Routing

records.text: Candace Owens said Superfeed Technologies owned the copyright to Turning Point USA's app and asserted that the app's user data therefore went to Superfeed.
records.speaker: Candace Owens

appearances.snippet: And Superfeed, by the way, read the fine print on Turning Point USA's app. Superfeed owns the copyright, which means that's where your data is going.

verification.notes: Current app-store and AP records confirm that Superfeed Technologies developed and publishes the TPUSA app, and Google Play discloses that the app collects and may share multiple data types. But copyright or developer status alone does not prove that all user data goes to Superfeed; that causal inference is broader than the disclosed evidence.
